definitions.explanation: A size that can be eaten in a single bite. Very common in cooking instructions and recipes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{一口大|ひとくちだい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧。
examples.english: Cut the vegetables into bite-sized pieces.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鶏肉|とりにく}→鶏肉：02919_toriniku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{一口大|ひとくちだい}にして⟦{下味|したあじ}→下味：06809_shitaaji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{付|つ}ける→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧。
examples.english: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and season it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{食|た}べやすい→食べやすい：21799_tabeyasui⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、{一口大|ひとくちだい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}って→切る：02693_kiru⟧⟦あげた→あげる：00546_ageru⟧。
examples.english: I cut it into bite-sized pieces so that the child could eat easily.

notes:
USAGE:
{一口大|ひとくちだい} is one of the most common instructions in Japanese recipes. It describes cutting food into pieces small enough to eat in one bite. The suffix {大|だい} here means "size."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一口大|ひとくちだい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ (to cut into bite-sized pieces)
- {一口大|ひとくちだい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to make bite-sized)
- {一口大|ひとくちだい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ちぎる (to tear into bite-sized pieces)

COMMON PATTERNS:
Used as a noun that modifies with ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧: 〜⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{一口大|ひとくちだい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧. The {大|だい} suffix meaning "size" also appears in words like ⟦{手|て}のひら→手のひら：05294_tenohira⟧{大|だい} (palm-sized).
